intro.title: Request Deduplication
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates request deduplication, a technique to prevent sending the same network request multiple times. You will learn how to use a JavaScript Map to track ongoing requests and ensure duplicate calls are avoided. The core concept involves checking if a request is already in progress before initiating a new one, improving performance and reducing server load. You will implement this using Vue's reactive state and computed properties to manage request statuses. By the end, you'll have a functional app that fetches data efficiently without redundant API calls.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is essential in modern web applications where multiple components might trigger the same API call simultaneously. In a Vue dashboard displaying real-time analytics, multiple widgets could request the same user data, causing unnecessary network traffic. This pattern prevents duplicate requests when users rapidly click search buttons or apply filters in data tables. It's also crucial in e-commerce product listings where sorting and filtering actions shouldn't trigger redundant API calls for the same product data.
